submission.natural_language_explanation: A context-free token detector for the lemma HAVE: it fires on the current token whenever that token is a form of 'have', strongest on ' have'/'have' (~2.2, regardless of auxiliary vs possessive use or subject), slightly weaker on ' has' (~2.0) and ' had' (~1.8), weaker on ' having', "'ve", capitalised 'Have' (~1.5) and on the negative contractions ' hadn' (~1.2), ' hasn' (~1.0), ' haven' (~0.9); it is near zero on every other token, including synonyms (' own', ' hold') and look-alike words (' behave', ' save').
rival_explanations: It is a present-perfect auxiliary detector that fires only on 'have'/'has'/'had' when followed by a past participle, not on possessive or standalone uses.
It is a general auxiliary-verb detector that fires on all auxiliaries ('have', 'has', 'had', 'is', 'was', 'will', 'would'), not specifically the HAVE lemma.
